payload.explanation: All 4 public tests pass. The patch correctly fixes all four seeded defects: (1) replaced permissive Number() parsing with /^\d+$/ so signed, fractional, exponent, hex, and empty values return null; (2) added Math.max(0, dateMs - nowMs) clamp for HTTP-dates; (3) changed attempt validation from Number.isFinite to Number.isInteger, correctly rejecting floats/NaN; (4) corrected backoff formula to 1000*2^(attempt-1). Non-string returns null, nowMs finiteness enforced for both functions, cap of 300000 applied to all returns, and very large attempts yield Infinity->min->300000 (finite capped). Change is confined to the single allowed file using only Node built-ins, keeping the public API unchanged. Clear, minimal 4-line semantic diff.
concerns: Date.parse is engine/locale dependent for some non-standard formats, though acceptable per the contract which explicitly relies on JavaScript Date parsing
No explicit rejection of NaN nowMs beyond Number.isFinite (handled correctly, but relies on that check for the HTTP-date path)
